questions.q: What does the GPU-Util percentage in `nvidia-smi` output actually represent?
options: The percentage of the GPU's theoretical peak FLOPs currently being achieved
The fraction of the last sampling period during which at least one kernel was executing on the GPU
The percentage of GPU memory currently allocated
The percentage of CUDA cores that are compute-bound
questions.explain: GPU-Util reports the fraction of the sampling period with some kernel running — it says nothing about how efficiently that kernel used the hardware.

questions.q: In the Processes section of `nvidia-smi` output, what information is shown?
options: A list of every file the GPU driver has open
The PID, process name, and GPU memory usage of each process using the GPU
A history of every kernel launched in the last hour
The compute capability of the GPU
questions.explain: The Processes table maps GPU memory consumption back to the specific host PID and process name responsible for it.

questions.q: What's the main advantage of `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=... --format=csv` over the default table output?
options: It runs faster on the GPU itself
It outputs structured, parseable rows instead of a boxed table, making it suitable for scripts and logging
It shows per-kernel occupancy data the default table doesn't
It permanently changes the GPU's power limit
questions.explain: The CSV query format avoids parsing box-drawing characters and gives clean, structured output, which is why monitoring scripts typically use it instead of the default table.

questions.q: A GPU shows 97% utilization in `nvidia-smi` the entire time a training job runs. What can you conclude?
options: The kernel is definitely compute-bound and running at peak efficiency
Only that some kernel was running during most of the sampling period — it could still be a badly memory-bound kernel wasting most of its cycles waiting
The GPU has run out of memory
The job is using multiple GPUs
questions.explain: GPU-Util only means something was executing; it does not indicate whether that execution was compute-bound, memory-bound, or efficient at all.

questions.q: Why would you reach for Nsight Systems or Nsight Compute instead of relying only on nvidia-smi?
options: nvidia-smi only reports device-wide, time-sampled numbers and cannot isolate a specific kernel's occupancy or throughput
nvidia-smi cannot be run on Linux
nvidia-smi requires a paid license to view memory usage
Nsight tools replace the need for a GPU driver
questions.explain: nvidia-smi gives a device-wide snapshot; it can't break performance down per kernel. Nsight Systems and Nsight Compute provide that finer-grained analysis.
